summary: This is a tag manager tool for Markdown blog files that can list, delete, rename, and suggest tags in article front matter. It detects duplicate tags (case variations and similar names), provides merge suggestions using heuristics like singular/plural matching, and delegates AI-powered tag suggestions to Node.js scripts. The tool preserves YAML formatting when writing files back and uses colored console output for readability.

explanations.11: oyaml is imported as 'yaml' — it's a YAML library that preserves key ordering when reading/writing, unlike the standard library's PyYAML.
explanations.12: frontmatter is a library that splits Markdown files into their metadata header (front matter) and content body, making it easy to read and modify tags.
explanations.30: This sets a threshold — if two tag names differ by 3 characters or less and one is a substring of the other, they'll be suggested as candidates to merge.

explanations.50: This custom function tells the YAML dumper to write Python lists in flow style (inline brackets like [a, b, c]) instead of block style (bullet points).
explanations.54: This custom function prevents YAML from automatically wrapping long single-line strings across multiple lines — it keeps them on one line.

explanations.74: StringIO is a utility that lets you write to a string as if it were a file, useful for capturing the YAML output before wrapping it with the front matter markers.
explanations.104: Counter is imported from collections and used here to tally how many times each tag appears across all files.

explanations.158: Python's sort is stable, so this first sorts by tag name alphabetically; then the next line re-sorts by count without disturbing the name order for ties.
